title: DC-area forecast: A comfortable evening and super Labor Day, then warming through midweek
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Partly cloudy with comfortable evening readings in the 70s dipping to sunrise lows within a few degrees of 60.

What's next? Labor Day is a lot like today. Trending warmer Tuesday through Thursday with only a slow rise in humidity. A chance for showers and storms could return Thursday as a front approaches.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: It's a great evening to enjoy the extended weekend outdoors — perhaps at a fire pit — as readings fall through the 70s. Skies become mostly clear by late evening and overnight lows dip to within a few degrees of 60. Confidence: High

Tomorrow (Labor Day): High pressure settles in overhead, bringing plenty of sunshine and continued comfortable humidity. Highs are within a few degrees of 80. Enjoy! Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Any early clouds should clear fairly quickly, leaving a great evening to be out and about as temperatures drop back through the 70s. Overnight lows again within a few degrees of 60. Confidence: High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Mostly sunny and a bit warmer Tuesday with highs back in the mid- to upper 80s, but humidity stays on the low side. Partly cloudy Tuesday night with lows in the 60s. Confidence: High

Feeling more like summer Wednesday and Thursday with highs in the upper 80s to near 90 under partly to mostly sunny skies. Humidity is up a bit by Thursday, when an approaching frontal boundary could bring a chance of showers and storms. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 9/10: Not a gripe in sight with plenty of sun and a less humid feel. Enjoy!| 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for September 6

Tropical systems shaped this date, with Hurricane Fran’s remnants in 1996 bringing flooding and damage, and Tropical Storm Hanna in 2008 setting a rainfall record and soaking the region.
